reason: The hypothesis directly mirrors the findings of E1, which explicitly states that trace interstitials cause phase segregation and softening upon aging at 700°C in a Ti-V-Nb-Ta alloy. E2 discusses strain softening in RHEAs but does not address the impurity mechanism, and it is cited as conflicting evidence without contradicting the core premises.
premises: Trace interstitials (O, N) contribute to solid solution strengthening in RHEAs.
Thermal aging at 700°C causes segregation of these interstitials.
Segregation depletes the matrix of solute interstitials.
Depletion of interstitials leads to progressive mechanical softening.
